message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine appropriate charge(s) for the given fact.

Fact: Tianjin Baodi district. On Nov 7 2016, at 12:00, defendant Yang 1, to vent emotions, set fire to corn husk and corn cobs in a colored steel house (a shed) belonging to his ex-wife Li 2, located at address. Then went to the main house, set fire to clothes in a wardrobe, causing fire in the main house roof and facilities, extinguished by fire brigade. Damage value 17905 yuan. After, defendant voluntarily surrendered and confessed.

So the crime is arson (setting fire intentionally). In Chinese criminal law, the charge is "放火" (arson) or "故意毁坏财物" (intentional destruction of property). In examples, they differentiate: "故意毁坏财物" for property damage without fire? Example: first case: multiple breakings of hotel items, damage 3166 yuan => "故意毁坏财物". For fire cases, they used "放火". Example: second case: using lighter to set fire in dorm, causing fire, they labeled "放火". Third case: farmer lighting grass causing fire, they labeled "失火". Wait "失火" is for accidental fire (unintentional). In that case, the farmer used lighter to ignite grass, causing fire, but maybe considered accidental? Actually they said "在未经县级以上林业主管部门审批同意的情况下...点燃杂草后引发火灾". That is considered "失火" (unintentional fire). So "放火" is intentional arson. Another example: Wu case: used lighter to set fire to house to drive away intruders, labeled "放火". So our case is intentional arson. So charge: "放火". Also maybe "故意毁坏财物"? But they used "放火" for intentional fire. So answer: [罪名]放火<eoa>.

Check list: "放火" is present. So final answer: "放火".
